scenes.headline: How OpenMuse swaps its agent, and what stays behind
scenes.sub: CopilotKit's self-hostable personal agent, read from its repository.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pecan! OpenMuse is a self-hostable personal agent that says it works with any harness. Here's how, and what stays behind.

scenes.text: OpenMuse doesn't integrate harnesses; it speaks AG-UI. Any agent that speaks it drops into one slot, but the tools and the approval gate stay behind.
scenes.say: OpenMuse doesn't integrate harnesses. It speaks one protocol, and any agent that speaks it too drops into a single slot.

steps.say: The app talks to a small server. One environment variable decides which agent answers.
By default, a built-in agent answers, and it brings twenty-nine tools: mail, browser, terminal, files.
Switch it to AG-UI, and any harness can answer: one request in, a stream of typed events back.

steps.note: the swap replaces conversational routing only
steps.say: But the tools live inside the agent it replaced, and the app draws eight cards by exact tool name. A swapped-in harness gets a chat pane, and no cards.

scenes.title: A card drawn by tool name
scenes.credit: OpenMuse's committed demo, cut and sped up

steps.say: Here's one of those cards, in the project's demo: a browser card with a live screenshot and a Take control button.
The mail and browser tools here are real, on a fictional mailbox. The model's replies are a mock.

scenes.label: is the whole swap: one branch that builds an AG-UI HttpAgent
scenes.note: the one harness adapter in the tree is disabled and connected to nothing
scenes.say: The portability is real: five lines. The one harness adapter in the tree is disabled and connected to nothing.

scenes.title: How a prepared email gets sent

items.say: The agent's strongest tools only prepare. A prepared email waits for approval, and there is no tool to approve it.

items.text: You approve in the app, by hash
items.say: The proposal is hashed over its input, connection and target. Approving presents that hash from the app, so approval binds to exactly what you saw.
One database update re-checks status, expiry and task state, so of two racing approvals, exactly one wins.

scenes.text: You can replace who does the talking. You cannot replace who holds the keys.

recap: One variable swaps in any AG-UI agent
Tools and cards stay with the built-in agent
Approval is hashed, bound, and needs a person
scenes.say: To recap: the talking is swappable. The tools, the cards and the approval gate are not.
